sections.h2: What is the quickest way to sell in Seguin?
sections.html:
Speed usually comes from a cash sale to an as is buyer, because that removes the lender, the appraisal and the repair list. A listing can bring a higher price, but it asks you to prepare the house, host showings and wait on a buyer's financing.

Seguin is the seat of Guadalupe County and sits on Interstate 10 and the Guadalupe River, about 35 miles northeast of San Antonio, per the Texas State Historical Association. That position gives the city both local buyers and people who commute toward San Antonio.

Decide first what you need: a fixed closing date, a clean break from a house with problems, or the highest price. Each goal points to a different sale method.

sections.h2: What shaped Seguin and its housing stock?
sections.html:
Seguin was laid out in 1838 as Walnut Springs and renamed in February 1839. It was incorporated on February 7, 1853, according to the Handbook of Texas, and it already had a school chartered in 1849. The Handbook says that schoolhouse was recognized by the state in 1962 as the oldest continuously used school building in Texas.

Older parts of town therefore include homes with a long history, and the Handbook mentions antebellum houses including the Sebastopol House State Historic Structure. Houses of that age tend to need roof, wiring or plumbing work, which a buyer will price in.

The local economy started in agriculture and trade, took a lift when oil was found in the Darst Creek fields in the late 1920s, and later added manufacturing and services. Texas Lutheran University, which moved to a farm near Seguin in 1912, adds a campus to the mix.

sections.h2: Which appraisal district and school district cover Seguin?
sections.html:
Guadalupe Appraisal District values property here, and its main office is in Seguin. Its member list includes the City of Seguin and Seguin ISD, which is the district most Seguin buyers will ask about.

The district runs an Appraisal Review Board that hears appeals, and a taxpayer liaison officer is on site on hearing days. Its site now offers online tools for homestead, disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, and printable forms remain available.

Who handles what for a Seguin parcel (Guadalupe Appraisal District and Texas Comptroller)

A mailing note from the district advises taking time sensitive mail to a post office counter for a manual postmark, since USPS processing changes in Texas can move the postmark date.

sections.h2: What permits does the City of Seguin require?
sections.html:
Seguin requires a permit to build, enlarge, alter, repair, move, demolish, roof or re-roof a structure, or to put in a fence. Its list of work that needs no permit includes painting, siding, window replacement in an existing single-family home or duplex, fences under seven feet and roofing above the deck.

The city lets a person who owns and lives in a homestead do the work personally with the proper permits, but the house must be registered as a homestead with the Guadalupe appraisal district. Hired work must go through a contractor registered with the city.

For a one or two family home, the approved final inspection report is the certificate of occupancy, and the city issues no separate paper. Call the permits office at 830-401-2435 if you are unsure whether past work was permitted. Seguin has adopted the 2021 International Residential Code and a Unified Development Code, plus a flood ordinance that follows FEMA guidance.

sections.h2: How do taxes, deeds and recording work for a Seguin sale?
sections.html:
Texas sets no statewide property tax. Values are fixed as of January 1, and bills go out in October with payment due on receipt. Most owners must pay by January 31, and February 1 starts penalty at six percent plus one percent interest.

Guadalupe County's clerk files deeds for land in the county, once a notary or similar officer has witnessed the signature. The Texas courts manual puts the first page at $5.00 and each added page at $4.00, plus a few other clerk fees, so ask the clerk for a current total.

  • General warranty, special warranty and quitclaim deeds are all recorded with the county clerk.
  • A trustee's deed follows a foreclosure sale; the sale is a public auction on the first Tuesday.
  • Liens for taxes can attach to the house, and a buyer cannot get clear title until delinquent taxes are paid.
  • Ask the title company for a payoff figure before you sign a contract.

sections.h2: What exemptions and caps should a Seguin seller know about?
sections.html:
A residence homestead in Texas carries a cap that limits how fast the appraised value can rise, no more than 10 percent a year, beginning the year after the owner first qualifies. Seniors and disabled owners also have a school tax ceiling that stays at the amount paid in the year they qualified, and it can follow them to a new Texas home in proportion.

Disabled veterans get exemptions by rating, from up to $5,000 at 10 to 29 percent up to $12,000 at 70 percent or more, and a veteran rated 100 percent may owe nothing on the homestead. Guadalupe Appraisal District has online tools for these exemptions, and the general filing deadline is before May 1.

For a seller these programs affect what a buyer will pay in tax. Someone buying after January 1 may request the exemption for the remainder of that year if the seller never had it. Heirs who are not on a recorded deed must give the district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill to claim the exemption.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, rented or hard to sell?
sections.html:
Inherited houses require clean paperwork first. A will can be probated within four years of death, and a muniment of title lets a will pass title when the estate has no debts besides real estate liens. Without a will, small estates of $75,000 or less, excluding the homestead, may use the small estate affidavit, which needs two disinterested witnesses and a court's approval.

If tenants live there, remember that Texas requires written notice to vacate before a justice court suit, normally three days, and the tenant has to be served at least four days before trial. After judgment a writ of possession is available six days later. Selling with the tenant still there avoids that process, though the lease terms then go with the house.

A house with deferred repairs is the simplest situation. A buyer taking the house as is handles the work, and you save on contractor bids.

faqs.a: The Guadalupe Appraisal District. Its office is in Seguin, and its website lists the City of Seguin and Seguin ISD among the units it serves.

faqs.q: Is a permit needed for Seguin window replacement?
faqs.a: Not for an existing single-family home or duplex, according to the city's no permit list. Roof work above the deck and painting are also on that list, but ask the permits office at 830-401-2435 when in doubt.

faqs.q: Is there a certificate of occupancy for a Seguin house?
faqs.a: For one and two family homes, the approved final inspection report acts as the certificate, and the city issues no separate document.

faqs.q: When must Seguin property tax be paid?
faqs.a: Most owners must pay by January 31. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Seguin house that is in probate?
faqs.a: Often yes, once the court has named someone with authority or the title has passed by muniment or affidavit. Ask a title company which path applies to your estate.
